{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a large, clear fish, and I built the upper tail lobe, which completes the tail and the fish's silhouette. I laid it, relaid it so it branches cleanly off the body line, and confirmed it is connected. By the final check, about 99 of the 101 standing dominoes were connected to the start domino, with both tail lobes included. The two loose dominoes near the join are not part of the outline.

Execution: I worked precisely on the fiddliest part of the build, the join where the tail meets the body. I inspected that area several times and traced the chain by eye from the nose. I reported accurately which pieces were dark and which were pale, and I closed the connection before time ran short. Once it was done, I kept my hands off the join so nothing could be bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I split the tail work cleanly with Priya, who took the lower lobe while I took the upper one. That let Maya stay on the top curve without interruption. I announced when I was working near the join and asked others to keep clear, so we avoided bumps. I also gave the table clear status updates, so everyone knew what was connected and when the fish was finished.

Leadership: I helped keep the table organized by proposing who takes the tail and when. I took ownership of the final connection and stayed with it until the whole chain was verified. At the end I helped the group agree to stop touching the build and protect the result.", "my_share_percent": 25}
